course.title: Strength Development
course.owner: JR Romero, CSCS - Director of Training
course.evidence_pack: G3-104 Strength Development Evidence Pack FINAL
course.purpose: Teach coaches to understand strength as a task-specific physical quality, develop it through defensible resistance-training decisions, measure it appropriately, and integrate it into athletic preparation without confusing gym performance with sport performance.
governing_distinctions: STRENGTH != POWER != RATE OF FORCE DEVELOPMENT
course.prerequisite: G3 102 and G3 103 complete including both terminal defenses; active G3 Performance coaching status
course.delivery: NovaKore self-paced modules with four observed practical sign-offs (PS-1 to PS-4) plus the final oral defense (T-01).

CO-3 Explain neural, morphological, technical, and connective-tissue contributors
CO-4 Select loading strategies appropriate to maximal-strength goals
CO-5 Explain why adaptation zones overlap
CO-6 Prescribe volume, frequency, rest, and effort without universal rules
CO-7 Decide when failure is or is not appropriate

evidence_classes.name: Established Evidence
evidence_classes.teaching_rule: May be taught as established, bounded by population and task.

evidence_classes.name: Supported Practice
evidence_classes.teaching_rule: Taught as well-supported practice with the moderator stated.

evidence_classes.name: Emerging / Conditional Evidence
evidence_classes.teaching_rule: Taught as conditional; never the sole basis for a required behavior.

evidence_classes.name: Applied Coaching Inference
evidence_classes.teaching_rule: Taught explicitly as inference, labeled aloud.

evidence_classes.name: Historical / Practitioner Framework
evidence_classes.teaching_rule: Taught as framework and history; never as proof.

evidence_classes.name: Unsupported / Overstated Claim
evidence_classes.teaching_rule: NEVER taught as true; used only to name and correct the error.

evidence_classes.name: Unresolved
evidence_classes.teaching_rule: Taught as an open question; may never anchor a required behavior or an assessment key.

unresolved_topics: open- versus closed-kinetic-chain superiority for athletic strength development
exact in-season microdosing dose rules for team-sport athletes
mechanism_association_transfer_rule: A mechanism explains how an adaptation could occur; an association shows two things vary together; transfer is a demonstrated change in the target task caused by the training. These are three claims with three evidence requirements, and a lesson may never present one as another.

doctrine.title: Strength Is Task-Specific
doctrine.statement: Strength must be interpreted relative to the task used to express or measure it. A barbell result is evidence of performance in that lift, not a complete measure of athletic strength.
doctrine.teaching_boundary: Does not devalue the barbell. Governs what may be concluded from a result, not whether it is worth testing.

doctrine.title: Strength Is Foundational, Not Sufficient
doctrine.statement: Strength supports many athletic outcomes, but increases in gym strength do not guarantee proportional improvements in sprinting, jumping, COD, or sport performance. Transfer depends on the athlete, task, training status, body mass, technical exposure, and surrounding program.
doctrine.teaching_boundary: Cuts both ways: 'get strong and everything follows' and 'strength doesn't transfer' are both unsupported.

doctrine.title: Adaptation Zones Overlap
doctrine.statement: Rep ranges and loading zones influence adaptation but are not discrete biological compartments. G3 rejects rigid rules such as '1-5 strength, 6-12 hypertrophy, 12+ endurance.'
doctrine.teaching_boundary: Overlapping is not identical; load still matters (D104-4). The rejection is of the boxes.

doctrine.title: Heavy Loading Is a Tool for Maximal Strength
doctrine.statement: Higher loads are generally effective for maximizing dynamic 1RM strength, but lower and moderate loads can still produce strength adaptation. G3 does not define strength training exclusively by heavy loading.
doctrine.teaching_boundary: No percentage, rep number, or loading table is published as a G3 rule. CA-01 and its mirror are both F.

doctrine.title: Failure Is Optional
doctrine.statement: Momentary muscular failure is not required for strength development. Failure may be used selectively when its benefits justify fatigue, technical, and recovery costs.
doctrine.teaching_boundary: 'Failure is necessary' and 'failure should never be used' are both F. No RIR target is published.

doctrine.title: Exercise Selection Is Constraint-Based
doctrine.statement: G3 does not prescribe universal 'best lifts.' Exercise selection reflects objective, athlete competence, anthropometry, loadability, stability, technical demand, fatigue cost, equipment, and transfer needs.
doctrine.teaching_boundary: Not a claim that all exercises are equivalent for an objective. No mandatory lift list exists in G3 104.

doctrine.title: Specificity Governs Modality
doctrine.statement: Free weights and machines, bilateral and unilateral exercises, dynamic and isometric methods, and full or partial ROM can all be useful. Their value depends on the adaptation and task, not ideological hierarchy.
doctrine.teaching_boundary: Four F claims corrected without inversion (CA-07 to CA-10); instability functionality also F. Open- vs closed-kinetic-chain superiority is U.

doctrine.title: Full ROM Is a Broad Default, Not a Law
doctrine.statement: Full ROM is a strong general default for broad strength development, while partial ROM can be used intentionally for joint-angle specificity, overload, progression, exposure, or contextual demands.
doctrine.teaching_boundary: 'On average' is taught explicitly. Partial ROM requires a stated rationale; 'sport-specific' alone does not qualify.

doctrine.title: Strength Programming Is Dose Management
doctrine.statement: Volume, frequency, intensity, rest, effort, and exercise selection interact. No single variable is treated as an independent universal prescription.
doctrine.teaching_boundary: No weekly set target, frequency prescription, or rest duration is published. The rest finding is directional, not numeric.

doctrine.title: Autoregulation Is a Decision Tool
doctrine.statement: RPE, RIR, APRE, VBT, and percentage-based methods are tools for prescription and adjustment. No one system is G3 doctrine or universally superior.
doctrine.teaching_boundary: 'VBT is inherently superior' is F; so is dismissing it. No velocity-loss threshold, zone, RIR, or RPE cut-point is published.

doctrine.title: Periodization Organizes Adaptation
doctrine.statement: Periodization is the purposeful organization of training variables over time. No single named periodization model is universally superior across athletes and contexts.
doctrine.teaching_boundary: Two findings held together: organizing beats not organizing; no organization wins. Named models are Class E.

doctrine.title: Concurrent Interference Is Conditional
doctrine.statement: Strength development can coexist with sprinting, conditioning, plyometrics, and sport practice. Interference depends on modality, dose, sequence, recovery, and athlete context rather than being inevitable.
doctrine.teaching_boundary: Concurrent evidence base is older and adult-weighted; no numeric spacing or sequencing threshold is created.

doctrine.title: Youth Can Train Strength
doctrine.statement: Properly supervised and progressively loaded resistance training is appropriate for youth. Readiness, technique, training age, maturation, supervision, and context matter more than outdated prohibitions based solely on chronological age.
doctrine.teaching_boundary: Claim is conditioned on supervision, technical coaching, and progression, stated every time. 'Technique first' must not become indefinite underloading.

doctrine.title: Standards Must Earn Their Authority
doctrine.statement: Universal bodyweight ratios, 'strong enough' thresholds, mandatory exercise prerequisites, and fixed asymmetry cutoffs are not treated as G3 scientific standards without adequate population- and outcome-specific evidence.
doctrine.teaching_boundary: Relative strength contextualizes; it may not gate a method. No replacement number is published.

doctrine.title: Safety Claims Require Evidence
doctrine.statement: No exercise is automatically safe or dangerous independent of loading, technique, athlete capacity, exposure, and context. G3 avoids simplistic claims about deep squats, knees-over-toes, deadlifts, or individual exercises 'preventing' injury.
doctrine.teaching_boundary: Restraint runs both directions. G3 uses injury-risk-reduction language, not prevention guarantees. Binds marketing and parent communication.

applied_standards.title: Define the Strength Task
applied_standards.text: Every assessment or prescription identifies what form of strength is being trained or measured.
applied_standards.boundary_or_enforcement: strength_task and test_record require strength_expression and task

applied_standards.title: Match Load to Adaptation
applied_standards.text: Loading is selected for the desired adaptation and athlete. Heavy loading is prioritized when maximal dynamic strength is the main target, without making it the only valid loading strategy.
applied_standards.boundary_or_enforcement: no percentage, rep number, or loading table published (CJ-09)

applied_standards.title: Preserve Technical Quality
applied_standards.text: Load progression is subordinate to acceptable execution, task intent, and athlete readiness.

applied_standards.title: Use Failure Deliberately
applied_standards.text: Failure is not a default requirement. Its use accounts for exercise complexity, athlete experience, fatigue cost, recovery, and session purpose.
applied_standards.boundary_or_enforcement: no RIR target or proximity rule published (CJ-04)

applied_standards.title: Exercise Categories Before Exercise Dogma
applied_standards.text: Coaches select movement and exercise categories and constraints before declaring individual exercises mandatory.
applied_standards.boundary_or_enforcement: naming a specific lift as mandatory fails production review

applied_standards.title: Use ROM Intentionally
applied_standards.text: Full ROM is the broad default where appropriate. Partial ROM requires an explicit rationale rather than a generic 'sport-specific' claim.

applied_standards.title: Rest to Preserve the Intended Output
applied_standards.text: For demanding strength work, rest generally supports force output and technical quality. Exact rest intervals remain contextual.
applied_standards.boundary_or_enforcement: criterion is output, not the clock (CJ-03)

applied_standards.title: Frequency Organizes the Dose
applied_standards.text: Frequency is used to distribute volume, technical exposures, fatigue, and recovery. It is not prescribed as an isolated magic variable.

applied_standards.title: Autoregulate With Known Limits
applied_standards.text: If RPE, RIR, VBT, or APRE are used, coaches must understand measurement error, athlete skill, exercise specificity, and the decision being informed.
applied_standards.boundary_or_enforcement: no threshold, zone, or velocity-loss figure published (CJ-05 to CJ-07)

applied_standards.title: Test the Construct
applied_standards.text: 1RM, submaximal RM, isometric tests, dynamometry, and velocity estimates measure different expressions of strength. G3 labels results according to what was actually measured.
applied_standards.boundary_or_enforcement: test_record requires construct_measured; mislabeling is a scored error

applied_standards.title: Avoid Universal Ratio Thresholds
applied_standards.text: Relative-strength metrics may contextualize athlete performance, but universal bodyweight ratios cannot automatically gate advanced training methods.

applied_standards.title: Interpret Asymmetry Cautiously
applied_standards.text: Asymmetry values require reliable measurement, task context, repeated observation, and athlete-specific interpretation. A single fixed percentage does not automatically mandate correction.
applied_standards.boundary_or_enforcement: no threshold published; local adoption requires Director of Training approval and a measurement-error basis (CJ-18)

applied_standards.title: Youth Training Requires Qualified Supervision
applied_standards.text: Youth resistance training is technically coached, progressively dosed, developmentally appropriate, and supervised.
applied_standards.boundary_or_enforcement: supervision ratio documented for every youth group; safety claim stated with conditions

applied_standards.title: In-Season Strength Is Constraint-Driven
applied_standards.text: In-season strength decisions protect meaningful exposure while adapting volume and frequency to sport load, competition density, recovery, and priority.
applied_standards.boundary_or_enforcement: no maintenance dose or microdose model published (CJ-16, CJ-17)

claim_audit.taught_instead: Higher loads generally maximize dynamic 1RM; lower and moderate loads still build strength, especially at high effort.
Adaptation zones overlap; the repetition continuum is too rigid.
Hypertrophy may support force capacity; value judged on contribution, not ideology.
Mass has consequences in tasks the athlete must move; a programming consideration, not an automatic penalty.
Failure is not required for strength or hypertrophy gains.

claim_audit.claim: Training to failure should never be used
claim_audit.taught_instead: Failure is a deliberate tool with real costs; selective use is defensible.
Both modalities effective; differences tend to reflect the testing modality.
Machines are a valid tool judged on the adaptation produced.

claim_audit.claim: Unilateral training is inherently more athletic
claim_audit.taught_instead: Both improve strength and athletic outcomes; specificity explains differences.
As above, in the opposite direction.

claim_audit.claim: Unstable surfaces are inherently more functional
claim_audit.taught_instead: Instability work is not inherently more functional for athletic strength development.

claim_audit.claim: Deep squats are inherently bad for knees
claim_audit.taught_instead: Review-level evidence does not support inherent harm to healthy knees with appropriate technique and loading.

claim_audit.claim: Knees should never pass the toes
claim_audit.taught_instead: The prohibition is not supported by the current evidence set.
Exact safety comparisons are U - Unresolved; no exercise is dangerous independent of context.
Progressive loading is appropriate when competence, readiness, and supervision support it.
Current evidence does not support the claim; supervised, progressed training is safe and effective.

claim_audit.claim: Olympic lifts are required for athletes
claim_audit.taught_instead: No lift is mandatory; selection is constraint-based.
Contraction-mode specificity, not universal superiority; costs must be accounted.

claim_audit.claim: Time under tension determines strength development
claim_audit.taught_instead: Deliberately slow tempo is not inherently better for maximal strength; concentric intent is more relevant.
Variation serves adaptation; novelty is not a mechanism.
Constant variation is unsupported and obstructs evaluation of adaptation.
Soreness is not an outcome measure.

claim_audit.claim: More volume always means more strength
claim_audit.taught_instead: Volume links more clearly to hypertrophy than to maximal strength; physique set rules do not import.
Strength is foundational, not sufficient; transfer is conditional.

claim_audit.claim: Every athlete needs a 2x bodyweight squat
claim_audit.taught_instead: Universal ratios are unsupported as predictors and may not gate methods.

claim_audit.claim: Asymmetry above 10% is automatically a problem
claim_audit.taught_instead: No single threshold is justified; interpretation requires measurement, context, and repetition.
VBT can improve outcomes; comparative evidence does not establish programming superiority.

claim_audit.claim: Women require fundamentally different strength principles
claim_audit.taught_instead: Foundational principles do not require a separate system; individual differences and evidence underrepresentation are both disclosed.

claim_audit_symmetry_rule: Every correction is a correction, not an inversion. Correcting a Class F claim by asserting its opposite reproduces the error.

competencies.title: Strength terminology
competencies.observable_standard: Names the strength expression, task, and metric in every claim; never collapses strength, power, and RFD.

competencies.title: Adaptation mechanisms
competencies.observable_standard: Gives a multifactorial account of a strength change and distinguishes mechanism from outcome.

competencies.title: Strength-to-performance transfer
competencies.observable_standard: States what strength-performance evidence licenses; distinguishes association from transfer; states a transfer pathway.

competencies.title: Loading selection
competencies.observable_standard: Selects loading for a named adaptation and athlete, without a rep-range rule or universal percentage.

competencies.title: Volume/frequency/rest management
competencies.observable_standard: Sets four dose variables as interacting, with criteria and no imported figures.

competencies.title: Proximity-to-failure decisions
competencies.observable_standard: Decides failure use from complexity, experience, fatigue, recovery, and purpose; asserts no RIR rule.

competencies.title: Exercise selection
competencies.observable_standard: Selects from constraints and categories; substitutes preserving intended adaptation; asserts no mandatory lift.

competencies.title: ROM/method selection
competencies.observable_standard: Applies full ROM as default and justifies partial ROM specifically when used.

competencies.title: Eccentric/isometric application
competencies.observable_standard: Uses contraction-mode methods for stated specificity, with cost accounted and no superiority claim.

competencies.title: Autoregulation/VBT interpretation
competencies.observable_standard: Uses RPE/RIR/velocity within stated limits; imports no threshold; ties each input to a decision it can change.

competencies.title: Progression/periodization
competencies.observable_standard: Organizes training over time with a stated rationale; claims no universal model; defends stability as well as change.

competencies.title: Concurrent/in-season integration
competencies.observable_standard: Counts existing load, protects meaningful exposure, defines in-season success, asserts no microdose rule.

competencies.title: Youth strength coaching
competencies.observable_standard: Applies readiness reasoning, progresses load when competence supports it, states the safety claim with its conditions.

competencies.title: Strength testing
competencies.observable_standard: Selects construct-appropriate tests, records conditions, labels results by task, interprets inside error.

competencies.title: Standards/asymmetry interpretation
competencies.observable_standard: Refuses universal ratios and thresholds without substituting new ones; interprets asymmetry with measurement and context.

competencies.title: Safety/evidence boundaries
competencies.observable_standard: Distinguishes injury-risk reduction from prevention; identifies unsupported claims; corrects without inverting.

competencies.title: Programming defense
competencies.observable_standard: Defends a full strength prescription under questioning across the eight obligations.

modules.title: What Strength Actually Is
modules.framing_statement: "He's strong" is not a coaching statement.
modules.purpose: To install the vocabulary and the task-specific conception of strength the course depends on, and to end the habit of treating one lift result as a global athletic attribute.
objectives: M1.1 Define strength as capacity to produce force or torque under specified task constraints
M1.2 Distinguish the expressions of strength
M1.3 Distinguish force, impulse, power, and RFD
M1.4 Explain why a 1RM measures performance in that lift
M1.5 State task and metric whenever a strength claim is made

common_errors: Reporting a lift number as 'strength' with no task
Using power, strength, and RFD as synonyms

modules.title: How Strength Adapts

cases.title: Middle-School Athlete New to Resistance Training
cases.situation_summary: 12-year-old, no resistance-training history, group of 16 with one coach, two 50-minute sessions weekly. Parent asks whether lifting will stunt growth and cites a school coach who says children should not lift until they finish growing.
cases.decision_prompt: What does the program consist of, how does loading progress, and what do you tell the parent?
failure_modes: A mandatory-lift program for a novice
Failure work in a youth novice session
A supervision ratio that makes the safety claim untrue

cases.title: High-School Athlete With Low Relative Strength
cases.situation_summary: 16-year-old, two years inconsistent training, lowest lower-body results absolutely and relative to body mass, acceptable competence. Previous coach's report requires a 2x bodyweight squat before power work.
cases.decision_prompt: Is low relative strength the priority, what is the target, and what do you do with the previous coach's threshold?
failure_modes: Replacing it with a different ratio
Treating a norm table as the requirement
Gating power or plyometric work on a strength number
Prescribing heavy loading beyond competent execution
Assuming low relative strength is automatically the top priority

cases.title: Strong Athlete Whose Sprint and Jump Performance Has Plateaued
cases.situation_summary: 17-year-old, three years consistent strength training, steadily improving lifts, unchanged sprint and jump results over two years, 6 kg body-mass increase, dense practice, minimal sprint exposure, no speed or plyometric block in 18 months.
cases.decision_prompt: Is more strength the answer, and what is the plan?
failure_modes: Treating strength acquisition as the goal
Adding a new lift as the intervention

cases.title: In-Season Team-Sport Athlete
cases.situation_summary: Scholastic squad mid-season, twelve weeks remaining, five practices and one to two matches weekly, two 40-minute slots with one regularly lost. Sport coach asks whether strength work should stop; an assistant proposes daily ten-minute microdosing citing research.
cases.decision_prompt: What is the in-season plan, how is it dosed, and what do you say to both coaches?
failure_modes: Quoting a microdose prescription as research-backed
Failure work on complex lifts in a congested week

cases.title: Athlete Who Cannot Comfortably Use a Conventional Barbell Back Squat
cases.situation_summary: 18-year-old collegiate athlete, long femurs, limited comfortable bar placement, history of discomfort (not pathology) in loaded back squatting. A visiting coach says machines and unilateral work are not functional.
cases.decision_prompt: What does her lower-body strength program look like, and how do you answer the visiting coach?
failure_modes: Treating the back squat as mandatory
Describing alternatives as inferior or corrective
Claiming unilateral work is more athletic

cases.title: Coach Wants Every Set to Failure
cases.situation_summary: New G3 coach programs every working set to failure across all exercises including heavy compound lifts for a mixed scholastic group. Athletes report heavy soreness, two technical breakdowns on heavy lifts, attendance dipping.
cases.decision_prompt: What is the correction, and what do you say to the coach?
failure_modes: Publishing an RIR rule as the fix
Addressing the coach by seniority rather than evidence

cases.title: VBT-Heavy Program
cases.situation_summary: Program rebuilt around velocity devices: every main lift prescribed by velocity target, sets terminated at a fixed velocity-loss percentage from a published study, one back-squat load-velocity profile applied across all lower-body lifts, and a claim of objective superiority over percentage-based training.
cases.decision_prompt: What is defensible, what is not, and what is the rewrite?
failure_modes: Keeping the superiority claim in any hedged form
Applying one profile across exercises or athletes
Collecting data that changes no decision

cases.title: 12% Interlimb Asymmetry
cases.situation_summary: Single-leg countermovement jump screening returns a 12% interlimb difference, tested once, portable system, end of training week. No pain, no injury history, normal practice and competition performance, unremarkable bilateral results. A staff member flags a corrective block citing a 10% threshold.
cases.decision_prompt: Does this finding change the program?
failure_modes: Running a corrective block that displaces the actual priority

cases.title: Knees Over Toes / Deep Squat Is Dangerous
cases.situation_summary: A parent asks that her daughter not squat below parallel and that knees never pass the toes. A sport coach tells athletes deadlifts are dangerous for teenagers. The athlete squats competently to depth under moderate load with no discomfort; another athlete in the group cannot yet control depth under load.
cases.decision_prompt: What do you say, and what changes in the program?
failure_modes: Complying with the prohibition to avoid conflict
Asserting deep squats are safe for everyone
Claiming the deadlift question is settled either way
Treating an individual competence limit as a rule about the exercise
Answering the parent with a citation rather than a decision

sign_offs.title: Strength Prescription Fundamentals
observed_behaviors: Identifies the objective and strength expression unprompted
Chooses exercise, load, repetition structure, and rest for that objective and athlete
Explains the expected adaptation before the set
Preserves technical quality - progression visibly subordinate to execution
Distinguishes evidence from judgment when asked
Uses no universal rule, ratio, or imported number as justification
assessor_questions: What expression of strength is this set training, and in what task?
Why that load for this athlete?
What would make you stop the set or reduce the load?
Which part of that answer is evidence and which is your call?

sign_offs.title: Exercise Selection & Coaching
observed_behaviors: Selects exercises from athlete and task constraints, naming category and constraint
Coaches setup and execution to a standard that makes the adaptation achievable
Regresses or progresses appropriately, changing the right variable
Justifies ROM and modality in adaptation terms
Avoids mandatory-lift ideology and modality superiority language
Makes a failure-use decision or explains why failure is not used
assessor_questions: Why this exercise rather than the obvious one?
What is the category, and what would substitute for it?
Is this athlete near failure, and does that matter here?

sign_offs.title: Youth / Contextual Strength Coaching
observed_behaviors: Accounts for training age, readiness, and maturation in setup and coaching
Provides genuine technical instruction and maintains the documented supervision ratio
Selects loading and progression appropriate to competence and actually progresses load when competence supports it
Rejects unsupported youth restrictions accurately without inverting them
States safety boundaries in conservative causal language
Adapts the session to context without abandoning its objective
assessor_questions: What tells you this athlete is ready for more load?
What would you say to a parent who asks about growth?
What ratio are you running, and is that enough for what you are coaching?
What is the safety boundary on this exercise for this athlete?

sign_offs.title: Integrated Strength Program / Microcycle
sign_offs.function: completion requirement; requires four-week delivery window
observed_behaviors: Analyzes sport and training demands and states what the week already contains
Identifies the strength priority and what it costs
Integrates sprint, power, conditioning, practice, and competition demands
Manages fatigue visibly and adjusts when output or execution degrades
Defines response measures and adjustment logic in advance
Identifies which elements are Coach Judgment
assessor_questions: What is the strength priority this block, and what is it costing?
What told you to change the dose?
What does success look like for this block?
Which decisions would another qualified coach reasonably make differently?

terminal_defense.title: Strength Development Programming Defense
terminal_defense.format: 20-30 minutes with an approved assessor using the coach's own athlete and artifacts; assessor works the eight obligations in order and probes at least four
mandatory_probes: What expression of strength does this plan develop, in what task, and how will you know it changed?
Why this exercise and this load - and what would you use if the equipment weren't here?
Justify your volume, frequency, and rest. Which of those numbers is evidence?
Which part of what you just told me is evidence, which is G3 standard, and which is your judgment?
What would make you change this plan? Be specific.
Tell me what you would say to this athlete's parent about injury risk.
non_compensable_failures: cites a universal ratio, threshold, or mandatory lift as justification anywhere

assessment_system.design_rule: Applied competencies are never certified by multiple choice alone. No learner passes with a failing score in Application, Coaching, Evaluation, or Defense.

pass_standards.applied: at standard or better, one revision permitted

item_writing_rules: No item answerable from a single memorized sentence outside the knowledge band.
Every scenario item commits the learner before feedback.

No key may depend on a claim classified C, D, E, or U.
No key may require a Class F claim to be treated as true.

Where multiple answers are defensible, the item is a decision item scored on reasoning.
Every item carries module, competency, doctrine, applied standard, evidence class, level, and key source metadata.

citation_integrity_findings.finding: The Evidence Pack's inline citation tags do not resolve to its own source register: 81 distinct cite:NN values ranging to cite:163 against a 54-record library (S1-S54), with no mapping table supplied.
citation_integrity_findings.handling: Inline tags are treated as non-authoritative. Every claim is anchored to EP104-nn records matched by domain and population. No assessment key may depend on an inline tag. No G3 material may reproduce the inline tags as citations.
citation_integrity_findings.gate: Before external publication, the pack's tag-to-source mapping must be supplied or affected sentences confirmed as resting on their EP104 anchors alone.

citation_integrity_findings.finding: Some Evidence Pack statements have no corresponding itemized record. The instance identified in production is the eccentric-only contraction-mode claim used in M7.
citation_integrity_findings.handling: Carried at reduced confidence; never sole support for a required behavior; never an assessment key. Further instances are flagged to the Director of Training and given the same restriction. Substitute citations must never be attached.
citation_integrity_findings.gate: Resolve or rewrite before external publication.

population_transfer_limitations: healthy adults, often men, often non-athletes, dominate the prescription evidence
autoregulation and VBT studies frequently use trained adults and laboratory tasks
female-athlete evidence is underrepresented in multiple domains
several youth records are foundational but older position statements
some practitioner-facing records are narrative reviews
microdosing records are single primary studies, one of them plyometric rather than resistance training
research_gaps_taught: athlete-specific dose-response for volume, frequency, failure proximity, and maintenance
direct sport-transfer effects of specific exercise choices and ROM strategies
reliable asymmetry thresholds linked to performance or injury risk
exact in-season microdosing models in team sport

external_use_gate.gate_requirement: resolution of citation-integrity findings CI-a and CI-b

testing_governance.rule: WHAT THE TEST MEASURES != GLOBAL ATHLETIC STRENGTH

test_constructs.measures: maximal dynamic performance in that specific lift
test_constructs.does_not_establish: global athletic strength; capability in another lift

test_constructs.measures: task-specific performance at that repetition demand
a model-derived estimate with equation and error limitations
test_constructs.does_not_establish: a measured maximum; comparability across equations or exercises

test_constructs.measures: force at the tested joint angle and muscle length
a device-, exercise-, and profile-dependent estimate
test_constructs.does_not_establish: a transferable profile across lifts or athletes
athlete readiness; a standard; a gate

standardization: consistent equipment, setup, and conditions recorded at time of testing
body-mass normalization only where it answers the question asked
testing_governance.threshold_prohibition: G3 104 creates no universal 'strong enough' threshold, bodyweight ratio, or asymmetry cutoff. Local working figures are environment-scoped Applied Standards with population, measurement basis including error, review date, and Director of Training approval; never evidence-derived; never a gate.
testing_governance.reporting: Every output carries test, task, construct measured, conditions, and interpretation limits. No composite score, no automated prescription, no readiness threshold, no asymmetry alert.

established: supervised youth resistance training is supported
growth-stunting claims are not supported by current evidence
chronological age alone does not determine readiness
technique, maturity, training age, supervision, and context matter
progressive loading is appropriate when competence and readiness support it
youth do not require an entirely different physiology-based strength doctrine
exact maximal-strength testing prescriptions require contextual judgment
youth.binding_rule: 'Technique first' must not become indefinite underloading. Every youth program states an observable progression criterion and is reviewed against it.

female_athletes.position: Foundational strength-training principles do not require a separate female system. Female athletes may differ in absolute and relative performance and individual context. Menstrual-cycle evidence is not converted into deterministic phase-based programming rules. Individual response may justify individual adjustment on individual grounds. Underrepresentation is disclosed at the point of the claim.

population_governance.population_transfer_disclosure: Required at the point of the claim, not as an end-of-module disclaimer (inherited AS-103-12).

safety_governance.language_standard: G3 uses injury-risk reduction, not injury prevention, wherever a causal guarantee would otherwise be implied.
may_not_be_claimed: that any single lift prevents any injury
that strength alone eliminates injury risk
that deep squats are inherently harmful to healthy knees
that knees must never pass the toes
that unstable training is inherently more functional
that deadlifts are inherently dangerous, or that the question is settled in their favour
that any exercise is safe or dangerous independent of athlete, dose, technique, progression, and context
may_be_said: the program builds exposure and capacity progressively
resistance training contributes to injury-risk reduction as part of a broader strategy
a specific athlete's range, load, or exercise selection is set by their current capability
medical questions are referred to medical professionals; clearance is a precondition, not a programming decision
safety_governance.governance: All external copy referencing strength training and injury requires Director of Training approval under the Brand Standards.

progression_governance.no_universal_figures: None is prescribed as an independent universal figure (D104-9, CJ-01 to CJ-09).
progression_governance.change_governance: Inherited G3 102 Doctrine 12: change is justified by adaptation, stagnation, mastery, pain, response, schedule, phase objectives, progression needs, changing demands, or fit - not by elapsed time, boredom, or novelty.

practitioner_frameworks.framework: progressive overload traditions and DeLorme-derived progressions

No entity may expose an automated strength prescription, readiness threshold, asymmetry alert, composite strength score, or automated training-priority recommendation.

No field may store a G3-published universal bodyweight ratio, asymmetry threshold, weekly set target, rest interval, RIR target, velocity-loss threshold, VBT zone, maintenance dose, or microdose as a course constant.
A strength_task may not be flagged mandatory at course level. (AS-104-05)
Free text containing an injury-prevention guarantee pattern is flagged for review before publication. (D104-15)
Content objects tagged with a U topic cannot be attached to an assessment key.
